diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows \cite[Lemma 2.4]{dwivedi2024numerical} and adapts it to the two-dimensional setting.

issues.failure_explanation: The pointwise inequality is false even for \alpha=2. Take f=cos x, g=cos 2x. At x=\pi/3, LHS=(-\Delta)(fg)=-4.25 while RHS=2(f(-\Delta)g+g(-\Delta)f)=-2.5, so the inequality fails. The fractional Laplacian of a product is nonlocal and requires additional derivative terms; it cannot be bounded by this expression.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false pointwise estimate with a correct fractional product/commutator inequality (e.g., Kato-Ponce) and re-estimate the nonlinear term.
issues.overall_effect: The bound on the nonlinear term in the proof of conv_lemma is invalid, undermining the H^{1+\alpha} estimate, local convergence, and all results relying on them.
issues.title: False fractional product estimate
issues.why_classification: The main results may survive with a standard replacement inequality, but the proof requires a nontrivial re-estimate of the nonlinear term.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound \eqref{bd3} is only established for t\leq\bar T, not uniformly for all time. The continuation argument in Remark remk_extnsn assumes a global H^{1+\alpha} bound that is never proved. Thus the proof only gives local existence, not the global existence claimed in Theorem thm:exisuq.

failure_location.quote: Since the semi-discrete approximation is bounded on the $H^{1+\alpha}_{\mathrm{per}}$-norm uniformly in time \eqref{bd3}, we may repeatedly apply the local existence and uniqueness Lemma \ref{conv_lemma}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove a global a priori H^{1+\alpha} bound or restrict the theorem to local time.
issues.overall_effect: The global well-posedness claim in H^{1+\alpha} for all T is unsupported, and the global error estimate in thm:spectral_accuracy lacks the required uniform bound.
issues.title: Invalid global continuation for fZK solution
issues.why_classification: A central global existence claim is abandoned without a new global estimate; the continuation argument does not establish the stated result.

issues.failure_explanation: For \alpha=1, the space H^{1+\alpha}=H^2 in two dimensions does not embed into W^{1,\infty}. Hence \|\partial_{x_1}u_N\|_{L^\infty} is not controlled by \|u_N\|_{1+\alpha} uniformly in N. The same false embedding is used in the uniqueness proof for \partial_{x_1}(\bar u+\bar w).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For \alpha=1, use a stronger norm or a different argument controlling the derivative in L^\infty; for \alpha>1, the embedding H^{1+\alpha}\subset W^{1,\infty} is valid.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform H^{1+\alpha} bound and uniqueness in conv_lemma are unproven for \alpha=1, so the convergence and well-posedness results fail to cover the endpoint \alpha=1.
issues.title: Sobolev embedding misuse at alpha=1
issues.why_classification: The endpoint \alpha=1 is explicitly included in the main results; losing it requires a new argument or excludes an advertised regime.

issues.failure_explanation: The optimal projection error estimate and the time-derivative error estimate are key to the spectral convergence proof, but their proofs are omitted. The cited result is for a 1D Kawahara equation; adapting it to the 2D fractional ZK operator is nontrivial and is not demonstrated in the source.

failure_location.quote: The proofs of Theorem \ref{thm:proj_error} and Lemma \ref{lem:time_error} follow the approach developed by Deng \cite[Theorem 2.1]{deng2017optimal} for the Kawahara equation. ... For brevity and to maintain focus on the novel aspects of our spectral discretization for the fZK equation \eqref{eqn:fZK}, we omit the detailed proofs and refer readers to \cite[Theorem 2.1]{deng2017optimal} for the complete methodology.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide complete proofs of the modified projection error estimates adapted to the 2D fractional ZK operator, or cite a directly applicable result.
issues.overall_effect: The optimal error analysis in thm:spectral_accuracy relies on unproven projection estimates, so the claimed convergence rates are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Omitted proofs of modified projection estimates
issues.why_classification: The missing proof is a contained but nontrivial adaptation; the main convergence result could survive if the estimates are established.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the L^\infty norm of a derivative by the H^2 seminorm. In two dimensions H^2 does not embed into W^{1,\infty}; this requires s>2. Thus the estimate of the nonlinear term is invalid (for \alpha=1 even H^{1+\alpha}=H^2 is insufficient).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the correct embedding H^{1+\alpha}\subset W^{1,\infty} for \alpha>1, and provide a separate argument for \alpha=1.
issues.overall_effect: The error estimate in thm:spectral_accuracy is not established by the given proof.
issues.title: False Sobolev embedding in spectral error proof
issues.why_classification: For \alpha>1 the proof can be repaired by using a stronger norm already available; the \alpha=1 case needs extra work, so more than a minor fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = e^{-L t} \mathcal{N}\left( e^{L t} V(t) \right) =: \mathcal{F}(t, V(t)).
Under the regularity assumption, the constant in the $\mathcal{O}(\Delta t^5)$ term is bounded uniformly in $N$.

issues.failure_explanation: The transformed nonlinearity \mathcal{F}(t,V)=e^{-Lt}\mathcal{N}(e^{Lt}V) contains oscillatory factors with frequencies involving L, whose entries grow like N^{\alpha+1}. Time derivatives of \mathcal{F} therefore grow with N, so the RK4 local truncation error constant cannot be bounded independently of N. The proof ignores this explicit N-dependent time dependence.

failure_location.quote: where the constant $C$ depends on $\|u_0\|_{r}$, $\alpha$, and the final time $T$, but is independent of $\Delta t$ and $N$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either allow constants depending on N and derive a coupled space-time step-size condition, or use a time integrator whose error analysis accounts for the interaction-picture oscillations.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed O(\Delta t^5) local error with N-independent constant and the resulting overall error bound are invalid; the time-discretization error analysis does not support the advertised efficiency.
issues.title: Temporal truncation error constant falsely independent of N
issues.why_classification: The N-independence of the temporal error is a central advertised guarantee; repairing it requires a new error analysis and likely a different time-step restriction.
